segments.he: וְלֹא לָאִישׁ חֲזָקָה בְּנִכְסֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ וְכוּ׳. פְּשִׁיטָא – כֵּיוָן דְּאִית לֵיהּ לְפֵירָא, פֵּירָא הוּא דְּקָאָכֵיל!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «a man does not have» the ability to establish the «presumption» of ownership «with regard to his wife’s property» and a wife does not have the ability to establish the presumption of ownership with regard to her husband’s property. The Gemara asks: Isn’t this «obvious? Since he has» the right «to» enjoy «the profits» of her property while they are married, «it is» known «that» he is only «enjoying the profits» and that he has no claim to the field itself. On what grounds, then, would he establish the presumption of ownership?

moves.about: a husband has no chazaka in his wife's property

moves.summary: obvious, since he eats the produce anyway
moves.about: since the husband owns the usufruct, his use evidently is only of the produce
